title: Discrete-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution with uncertainty principle
authors: Jiale Mi, Yiming Bian, Song Yu, Zhengyu Li, Yichen Zhang, Hong Guo
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution is a compelling framework for scalable quantum networks due to its seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. However, a fundamental gap persists between theoretical protocols requiring ideal Gaussian modulation and the constrained, discrete-modulated signals dictated by practical high-speed hardware. Current security proofs for discrete modulation rely on semidefinite programming, which suffers from prohibitive computational overhead for high-order constellations and lacks direct physical insight into non-Gaussian modulation.In this Letter, we overcome this limitation by developing a security framework that obviates semidefinite programming in favor of an approach grounded fundamentally in the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. By introducing a multi-mode entanglement-source model to characterize non-Gaussian state preparation, we establish an explicit mapping between constellation geometry and the secret key rate. This framework effectively quantifies the security implications of hardware-limited, finite state preparation, enabling both numerical and analytical security analysis under high-order constellations. We experimentally validate our method on both discrete-component and integrated photonic platforms, demonstrating that a quadrature amplitude modulation format with 256 constellation points can asymptotically approach the Gaussian capacity limit. Beyond quantum key distribution, the principle of tightening uncertainty-constrained bounds via source-mode expansion offers a paradigm for exploring the information-theoretic properties of complex non-Gaussian systems.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, SDP-free security framework for discrete-modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution. By grounding the analysis in the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and utilizing source-mode expansion, the authors successfully quantify key rates for high-order constellations. The work is validated both theoretically and experimentally on photonic platforms, demonstrating strong noise resilience.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a secure key rate analysis framework for discrete-modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD) that avoids computationally prohibitive Semidefinite Programming (SDP).
main_result: The authors developed a security framework based on the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, enabling high-order constellation analysis and showing performance approaching ideal Gaussian limits with 256 points.
method: The method involves developing an entanglement-based security bound by introducing ancillary modes and employing symmetrization techniques to simplify the covariance matrix constraints, thereby obviating SDP.
model_or_system: The system is CV-QKD using discrete modulation, modeled via a multi-mode entangled source ($ho_{ACB}$) characterized by its covariance matrix. The analysis extends from theoretical bounds to experimental validation on both discrete and integrated photonic platforms.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), Covariance matrices ($\gamma_{ACB}$), Normalized SKR ($	ext{SNorm}_{BE}$).
important_parameters: Constellation size (up to 256 points), excess noise ($	ext{SNU}$), channel transmittance ($T$), and the degree of modulation order.
main_assumptions: The security analysis relies on exploiting the convexity of the Secret Key Rate (SKR) function, and experimental results assume successful implementation of advanced Digital Signal Processing (DSP).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the prepare-and-measure vs. entanglement-based schemes, show the three steps of covariance matrix symmetrization, compare SKR for different modulation orders (e.g., 256-QAM), and detail the experimental setup using chip-based photonics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the SDP limitation in CV-QKD security proofs to proposing a Heisenberg uncertainty principle-based framework. This is followed by detailed mathematical derivations involving multi-mode state symmetrization, culminating in both theoretical analysis and experimental validation across various modulation formats.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical limitations in quantum communication protocols by providing computationally tractable security bounds for real-world hardware constraints (discrete modulation), which is crucial for realizing scalable quantum networks.
